topic: snake shedding isn't about growth -- adult snakes still shed for mite removal and eye-cap health
title: A Fully-Grown Snake Still Sheds Its Skin — Here's Why
description: A snake's growth slows to almost nothing once it's an adult, yet it keeps shedding its entire skin every few months anyway. The real reason has more to do with mites, skin damage, and eyesight than size. Reptile keepers actually treat a clean shed as a health check, not just a growth spurt.

hook_candidates.text: Most people believe a snake sheds its skin to grow — but a fully-grown one that's basically stopped growing still does it every few months.
A snake that's basically stopped growing will still shed its entire skin every few months anyway.
If shedding is only about growing bigger, why does a snake that's stopped growing still do it every few months?
A shed snake skin does three jobs at once, and growing bigger barely makes the list.

payoff_mechanism: Snake skin can't stretch as the animal ages, so periodically shedding the entire outer layer scrapes off mites, repairs scarring, and swaps in a fresh clear eye cap, which is why the habit continues even once growth has nearly stopped.
share_trigger: Send this to the friend who owns a snake and thinks shedding just means it's still growing bigger.
contradicted_belief: Most people believe a snake sheds its skin only because it's still growing bigger.

sources.note: Confirms snakes are indeterminate growers that keep shedding a few times a year even once growth slows drastically.
Britannica's snake molting entry confirms shedding renews damaged/worn skin, not only skin outgrown by size.

beats.text: Most people believe a snake sheds its skin to grow — but a fully-grown one that's basically stopped growing **still** does it every few months.
Skin can't stretch as a snake ages, so shedding it scrapes off **mites** and heals scars underneath.
Snakes have no eyelids — the eye cap sheds too, and a bad one can leave a snake **blind**.
Keepers check every shed for two intact eye caps — a missed one can cost real **eyesight**.
Growth was never the reason — it's skin **maintenance**, mites and eyesight included, growth just tags along free. Follow for the one your biology teacher skipped.
